children: Zimbabwe-focused Duration Gold has signed an agreement with China Railway Resources Group to explore $600 million in  investments to revive and expand four gold mines in the African country, it said on Thursday.

CRRG CEO Shi Yuan and Duration Gold Managing Director Allan Dolan signed the agreement in Harare to advance discussions on jointly investing to develop four large-scale gold projects in Zimbabwe, Duration Gold said
CRRG intends to introduce AI-based, smart mining techniques to the proposed partnership, Shi said during the signing ceremony
CRRG, a wholly owned subsidiary of China Railway Group
, would also contribute financing, technology and engineering expertise to Duration Gold's exploration and mine development projects, Duration said
The planned investment covers Duration Gold's Vubachikwe, Gaika, Athens and Royal Family mines, brownfield assets with a history of gold production spanning several decades
CRRG's extensive assets include copper-cobalt operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo and a molybdenum mine in China
Zimbabwe's gold production has rebounded in recent years, as prices
that hit a record at the start of this year have driven investment
The southern African nation has more than doubled gold output over the last decade, producing a record 46.7 metric tons in 2025, with production projected to exceed 50 tons this year
